title: Increase device batch size to reduce grad-accum overhead
description: Tried DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128->256 (grad_accum_steps 4->2... actually 2->1); OOM'd at seq_len 2048. No valid intermediate value exists since DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE must evenly divide TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE/MAX_SEQ_LEN=256, so reverted to baseline 128 unchanged.
reflection: 128 is already the VRAM ceiling for DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at this seq_len/model size on this GPU -- 256 OOMs immediately during the forward pass (tried to allocate 512MiB with ~79GB already in use). Because TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE/MAX_SEQ_LEN=256 exactly, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE is constrained to divisors of 256 (128, 64, 32...), so there's no intermediate value like 192 to try -- it's a hard binary choice between 128 (fits) and 256 (OOM). This throughput lever is dead as proposed; don't retry it without also reducing TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE or adding activation checkpointing, which trades off against other things. Other agents proposing the same DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=256 idea should be warned before spending another run on it.
